capacity-mix: 2024 edition data, not updated. Ownership and provincial shares retain the 2024 comparison. The updated FY25 fuel mix appears below.
thermal: Updated to FY25. All labels are shares of total utility-scale capacity; rooftop solar is excluded. Rounded thermal fuel shares sum to 56%, compared with the reported headline of about 57%. The chart uses the components so its shares total 100%. RFO means furnace oil. The newer March 2026 total includes net-metered solar and is discussed separately.
geography: 2024 edition data, not updated. All four capacity and demand shares retain the 2024 comparison. North comprises Punjab and KPK; South comprises Sindh and Balochistan.
customers: Updated to FY25. The ten consumer counts total 40,435,207 connections, including K-Electric and excluding TESCO. Rounded shares sum to 99.8%; slice areas are normalised to that total. Connections are not people.
tariffs: 2024 edition data, not updated. The chart compares 2021 and 2024 tariffs. Consumer classes, taxes and exchange-rate dates are not harmonised, so these figures should not be compared directly with industrial tariff estimates.
bill: 2024 edition data, not updated. These are illustrative bill shares, not a current bill calculator. The updated Rs. 3.23/unit debt-service surcharge does not establish a new percentage split.
imports: 2024 edition data, not updated. The series covers 2004–2024; intermediate points are approximate readings of the historical chart. FY25’s approximately 29% includes RLNG, imported coal, furnace oil and electricity imports. Its broader definition prevents a direct extension of this series.
fuel-cost: Updated to October 2025, the latest comparable fuel-cost observation in the supplied update. These are monthly fuel costs, not complete tariffs or annual averages. HSD was not dispatched and is omitted, rather than shown as zero. The update cites a NEPRA decision dated 9 December 2025 but does not provide its direct link.
capacity: Updated to FY25 for installed capacity and served seasonal peaks. The dashed 23,000 MW average-demand line is 2024 edition data, not updated. Served peaks differ from NEPRA’s computed demand above 33,000 MW. Nameplate capacity is not continuously dispatchable spare power.
payments: 2024 edition data, not updated. Both ownership and capacity-payment shares retain the 2024 groupings. Current payment totals cannot be allocated using these historical shares.
losses: Updated to FY25 for the final bar: Rs. 265 billion in losses above allowed targets and Rs. 132 billion in under-recovery, excluding K-Electric. FY23–FY24 bars are 2024 edition data, not updated on a comparable basis. Later reports give different historical baselines and collection definitions, so the bars do not establish a comparable percentage decline. No FY26 performance series is supplied.
discos: Updated to FY25 using the supplied NEPRA performance-report figures. Financial losses measure breaches of allowed targets, not all lost electricity. The reported Rs. 265.01 billion total excludes K-Electric; the displayed companies do not reproduce the full aggregate. K-Electric’s Rs. 1.05 billion calculation is disputed. The 8% global reference is 2024 edition data, not updated.
benchmark: Updated to FY25 for Pakistan’s ex-WAPDA DISCO loss rate of 17.55%. Foreign rates and the 8% global reference are 2024 edition data, not updated; their underlying years and coverage are not harmonised. K-Electric’s separate FY25 rate is 14.73%.
debt: Updated endpoints: Rs. 2,393 billion in June 2024, Rs. 1,614 billion in June 2025 and Rs. 1,675 billion in June 2026. Another official reply reports Rs. 1,641 billion for June 2025. Earlier points are 2024 edition data, not updated; intermediate values are approximate chart readings. The September 2025 refinancing occurred after the June 2025 reduction.
markets: 2024 edition data, not updated. The historical comparison covers 1989 and 2024 and counts 230 jurisdictions in each year without defining coverage. Pakistan’s 2026 market opening is discussed separately.
transport: 2024 edition data, not updated. Vehicle counts and the 4,500 MW estimate describe an illustrative full-electrification scenario, not a forecast. Areas do not encode quantities. Actual demand and savings depend on adoption, charging patterns, efficiency and the generation mix.
sales: Updated: all FY21–FY25 observations use Economic Survey 2025–26, Statistical Appendix Table 14.1, including revised FY21–FY23 values. FY23 sales fell 3.3% for households and 1.5% for industry. July–March FY26 figures in the text are partial-year observations and are not joined to this annual series.
solar-prices: Updated for the reported 2026 range of 10–12 US cents per watt. The 28-to-11-cent comparison is 2024 edition data, not updated; its precise endpoint dates are not specified. The shaded range is not a confidence interval. Panel prices exclude inverters, installation and batteries.
solar-imports: Updated to January–May 2026, compared with the same five months of 2025. Imports fell from 11,781 MW to 4,574 MW, a 61% decrease after rounding. The chart converts MW to GW. These are imported module volumes, not installed capacity or full-year totals.
distributed-solar: Updated estimate, published June 2026. Includes modelled behind-the-meter generation. This is a generation share, not utility-scale installed capacity; the two charts use different denominators.
lng-exposure: Updated to the March 2026 IEEFA assessment, citing Kpler. These supplier shares measure imported LNG, not total gas use. Supplies from Qatar and the UAE depend on passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
fixed-cost-pressure: Illustration, not observed data or a forecast. Index = 100 × 100 ÷ units sold. A 20% fall in sales raises fixed cost per unit by 25% only if fixed costs are unchanged. Fuel savings, taxes, tariff design and changes to contracts are excluded.
climate-target: Policy target, not achieved reductions. The 17- and 33-percentage-point components together form a 50% reduction against projected 2035 emissions. The conditional component depends on international finance, technology transfer and capacity support; this does not show funding already raised.
battery-imports: Updated estimate, published July 2026. Uses the sector breakdown’s 1.43 and 4.59 GWh totals; the report rounds 2025 to 4.6 GWh and reports growth of about 220%. Cumulative imports over 2018–2025 were 7.6 GWh. Imports do not measure operating storage, and GWh is not interchangeable with GW.
solar-import-savings: Updated analysis published March 2026 and revised in April. The second figure assumes elevated fuel prices persist; it is not a realised 2026 result. The two periods differ, so these figures are shown separately rather than as an annual trend or a combined total.
